prompt: Which of the four boxes is billed for the resources inside it?
hint: One box holds identity and another holds money.

choices.text: The tenant
choices.why: The tenant holds identities. Nothing is billed to it.

choices.text: Each subscription, for what it holds
choices.why: Right. It is the box of money, and its quotas are counted in it.

choices.text: The root management group
choices.why: Management groups pass rules down; they are not billed.

choices.text: The resource group
choices.why: A group sorts resources inside a subscription; the bill is the subscription's.

prompt: What is the id of a tenant's root management group?
hint: The portal calls it Tenant Root Group.

choices.text: Always the string `root`
choices.why: No fixed string: the root is named after its tenant.

choices.text: The id of the first subscription created
choices.why: Subscriptions hang below the root; none of them names it.

choices.text: It is the tenant's own id
choices.why: Right. Which is why `tree.bicep` defaults its parent to `tenant().tenantId`.

choices.text: Whatever the person who signed up chose
choices.why: Nobody chooses it; it is created with the tenant.

prompt: `rg-shop-prod` was created in `brazilsouth`. A virtual machine in it is in `southcentralus`. What does the group's location decide?
hint: What does the group itself store?

choices.text: Nothing: the VM's creation should have been refused
choices.why: A group's resources may be in any region. Azure accepts it.

choices.text: That the VM is billed at São Paulo's prices
choices.why: A resource is priced by its own region, not its group's.

choices.text: The region the VM falls back to if Texas fails
choices.why: No such fallback exists; recovery is something you design.

choices.text: Where the group's own record is kept
choices.why: Right. Only the metadata lives there, which is why it should match the resources.

prompt: How many levels of management groups may a tenant have below its root, not counting the root or the subscriptions?
hint: The lesson gives the depth in words.

prompt: The shop's marketing department is split in two. Somebody proposes moving `shop-prod` under a new management group named after one of the halves. What does the lesson say against it?
hint: What does a branch of the tree exist for?

choices.text: Moving it changes the policies production inherits
choices.why: Right. A reorganisation would drag the policies of production with it.

choices.text: Management groups cannot be created after the first year
choices.why: They can be created at any time, up to 10,000.

choices.text: Marketing has no access to Azure, so the group would be empty
choices.why: Access is not what the tree is drawn from either.

choices.text: A subscription cannot be moved once placed
choices.why: It can be moved. That is the danger, not the protection.

prompt: Resource groups do not ___: a group cannot contain another group.
hint: A word for boxes inside boxes.

prompt: In `/subscriptions/bbbbcccc-1111-dddd-2222-eeee3333ffff/resourceGroups/rg-shop-prod/providers/Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks/vnet-shop-prod`, what is `Microsoft.Network`?
hint: It comes right after `providers`.

choices.text: The name of the network
choices.why: The name is the last piece, `vnet-shop-prod`.

choices.text: The namespace that owns the type
choices.why: Right. `Microsoft.Compute` owns machines, `Microsoft.Storage` storage accounts.

choices.text: The subscription's display name
choices.why: A subscription appears in an id by its GUID only.

choices.text: The region the network lives in
choices.why: A region is not part of a resource id at all.

prompt: `rid.py` printed the management group's whole id back as its `name`. Why?
hint: Where does that id start?

choices.text: The management group did not exist in the lab
choices.why: Nothing exists in the lab; the parser only reads strings.

choices.text: The id was mistyped
choices.why: It is the correct form of a management group's id.

choices.text: The parser expects a subscription in it
choices.why: Right. Things above every subscription have ids that start at `/providers/`.

choices.text: Management groups have no names, only ids
choices.why: `mg-shop` is its name; the parser just did not find it.

prompt: A cleanup script keeps a list of ids it has already deleted and skips any id `==` one in the list. It deletes `.../resourceGroups/rg-shop-prod/...` and later meets `.../resourcegroups/RG-SHOP-PROD/...`. What happens?
hint: Who compares ids ignoring case, and who does not?

choices.text: It deletes the same group twice
choices.why: Right. The two strings differ, so the script treats them as two resources.

choices.text: Skips it: Azure ignores case
choices.why: Azure ignores case; the script's `==` does not.

choices.text: Azure refuses the second id as malformed
choices.why: Azure accepts either spelling as the same resource.

choices.text: The parser corrects the case before comparing
choices.why: The parser returned the pieces exactly as typed.

prompt: Match each name rule to an example of it.
hint: One rule exists because the name becomes an address.

pairs.right: two groups called `rg-shop-prod` in one subscription

right_distractors: the display name shown in the portal

prompt: Under the naming convention this course uses, what is `snet-app`?
hint: Read the prefix.

choices.text: The app's subscription network
choices.why: A subscription has no network of its own; a network lives in a group.

choices.text: A service endpoint for the app
choices.why: Endpoints are lesson 19 and have prefixes of their own.

choices.text: A storage network share
choices.why: Storage accounts take no dashes at all.

choices.text: A subnet for the application
choices.why: Right. `snet-` is the prefix for a subnet.

prompt: A management group's id starts with `/___/Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/`, with no subscription in it.
hint: The same word sits before every namespace in an id.

prompt: What does `az bicep build` produce from a `.bicep` file?
hint: It is what Resource Manager receives.

choices.text: A running resource in a sandbox subscription
choices.why: Building sends nothing to Azure.

choices.text: A Terraform configuration of the same resources
choices.why: Bicep compiles to Azure's own format, not Terraform's.

choices.text: An ARM template, in JSON
choices.why: Right. The same document a deployment would send.

choices.text: A plan of what would change in the subscription
choices.why: Comparing against what exists needs Azure; that is `what-if`, lesson 26.

prompt: `wrong.bicep` has no `targetScope` line. Where is it aimed?
hint: The compiler said so in its refusal.

choices.text: At a resource group, where a file with no scope aims
choices.why: Right. `Scope "resourceGroup" is not valid for this resource type.`

choices.text: At whichever subscription is signed in
choices.why: The scope is fixed in the file, not by who deploys it.

choices.text: Nowhere, until a scope is given on the command line
choices.why: The file has a scope even when it does not say one.

choices.text: At the tenant
choices.why: The tenant is chosen with `targetScope = 'tenant'`.

prompt: In the compiled `tree.bicep`, the parent of `mg-shop-prod` is `[tenantResourceId(...)]` rather than an id. Why?
hint: Who knows the tenant's id?

choices.text: The compiler could not find `mg-shop` and left a placeholder
choices.why: It found it: the expression names it.

choices.text: Resource Manager evaluates it when the template arrives
choices.why: Right. Only Resource Manager knows the values; the compiler fixes the shape.

choices.text: Bicep hides ids so that templates can be shared
choices.why: Nothing is hidden; the value just does not exist yet.

choices.text: Management groups have no ids until they have subscriptions
choices.why: A management group has an id from the moment it exists.

prompt: Match each resource to the scope a deployment of it is aimed at.
hint: Each box is created from the box above it.

prompt: `az deployment sub create --location brazilsouth --template-file rg.bicep` creates a group whose own `location` is set in the file. What is the `--location` on the command line for?
hint: What has no location of its own?

choices.text: It overrides the location written in the file
choices.why: The file's value stands; the flag is about something else.

choices.text: It sets the default for resources created later
choices.why: That is `AZURE_DEFAULTS_LOCATION`, a CLI setting.

choices.text: It is the region the subscription is billed in
choices.why: A subscription is not billed by region; resources are priced by their own.

choices.text: It locates the deployment's own record
choices.why: Right. A subscription has no location, so the deployment needs to be told one.

prompt: `terraform validate` passed and `terraform plan` failed with *Please run 'az login'*. What does that pair show?
hint: Which of the two needs to ask Azure anything?

choices.text: The configuration has an error that only `plan` detects
choices.why: `plan` never got as far as the configuration; it stopped at the sign-in.

choices.text: Terraform needs Bicep to be installed to plan
choices.why: Terraform does not use Bicep at all.

choices.text: The provider was downloaded but not installed
choices.why: `init` installed it, and `validate` used it.

choices.text: Shape is checked here; comparing needs an identity
choices.why: Right. The same line Bicep draws.

prompt: Put the pieces of a subnet's resource id in the order they appear, from the left.
hint: From the outermost box inwards.
trap: The subnet comes last because it is a child of the network.

prompt: A colleague says: "Our Azure account is the subscription, so our users live in it." What is wrong with the sentence?
hint: Which box holds identities?

choices.text: Users live in the root management group
choices.why: Management groups hold subscriptions, not users.

choices.text: Nothing: users are created inside each subscription
choices.why: A subscription trusts a tenant for its identities; it holds none.

choices.text: Users live in the tenant the subscription trusts
choices.why: Right. Identity is the tenant's box and money the subscription's.

choices.text: Users live in a resource group of their own
choices.why: A resource group holds resources; an identity is not one of them.

prompt: Which of these can the lab check without an Azure account? Choose all that apply.
hint: What did the lesson's commands answer, and what did they refuse?

choices.text: That a resource is aimed at a scope where it can be created
choices.why: Right. `BCP135` was that check.

choices.text: That every block of a Terraform file matches the provider's schema
choices.why: Right. `terraform validate`.

choices.text: That `rg-shop-prod` does not yet exist in the subscription
choices.why: Only Resource Manager knows what exists.

choices.text: The pieces of a resource id
choices.why: Right. An id is a string, and `rid.py` cut it up.

choices.text: Which management group a subscription is in today
choices.why: That is a question about Azure now, which needs a sign-in.
